chapter: Harlem, race and life in Europe
title: No racial prejudice and the luck of making a living in jazz
summary: Freeman says his prejudices were never racial and he never dreamed he could make a living playing this music.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well, it's a shame really to see what is going on. I don't get into these issues because I know what my life has been. I know that I can honestly say that my prejudice never went to anything racial. I think my prejudices were always personal. We are all prejudiced in some way and about something, obviously, but it was not possible for me to have it since I admired the black musicians so much and loved the music so much. And made a life -- you know, I didn't really know, Helen, when I first heard this beautiful music that
I was going to be able to make a living trying to play like that. It was such an esoteric kind of thing, you see I never dreamed.
